text: THE DAILY BRIEF: AI-POWERED NEWS PLATFORM

Good morning or afternoon. I am Mansi Saxena. My project is The Daily Brief, an AI-powered news platform. I will explain why I built it, how the system works, and what readers and writers can do with it. The live project is available at https://the-daily-brief-beige.vercel.app/.

name: text
text: THE DAILY BRIEF: AI-POWERED NEWS PLATFORM
I will begin with the project background and problem. Then I will cover the technology, main features, benefits, current limits, and future improvements.

name: text
text: THE DAILY BRIEF: AI-POWERED NEWS PLATFORM

name: text
text: A website for reading news and sharing articles written by users.

name: text
text: Browse stories from eight categories, trending articles, and search results.

name: text
text: Get a short summary or help prepare an article.

name: text
text: Follow writers, save stories, listen, like, share, and report concerns.

The Daily Brief brings news browsing and community publishing into one site. Readers can explore eight categories, search for stories, and read articles written by users. AI can summarize articles and help writers prepare their work.

name: text
text: THE DAILY BRIEF: AI-POWERED NEWS PLATFORM

name: text
text: A large news feed can make it hard to choose what to read first.

name: text
text: Readers may want the main points before reading the full story.

name: text
text: New writers may need help organizing an article clearly.

name: text
text: Harmful content and claims that may be false need careful review.
The project responds to four needs: choosing from a large amount of news, understanding long stories quickly, helping people structure articles, and reviewing content concerns.

The solution combines category news, AI summaries, and reader-written articles. Writers can start with a topic or a draft and edit the result. The site also supports reader actions and admin review of posts that need more attention.

Readers can browse and search stories across different sources, including posts written by users. They can generate an AI summary, listen to a full article, save it, like it, share it, follow its author, or report a concern.

Writers can submit a manual draft or create a first draft from a topic. In topic mode, the system checks its existing knowledge before deciding whether to search the web. The writer edits the preview and can add an image. AI screening and admin review help manage posts that need attention.

name: text
text: THE DAILY BRIEF: AI-POWERED NEWS PLATFORM

The website uses Next.js, React, and TypeScript. Tailwind CSS styles the pages. MongoDB stores account and article data, while GridFS stores article images. OpenAI provides summaries, writing help, and content screening. Google News RSS supplies external news links.

name: text
text: THE DAILY BRIEF: AI-POWERED NEWS PLATFORM

name: text
text: Next.js and React show pages for browsing, search, and articles.

name: text
text: Server routes handle sign-in, writing, summaries, moderation, and reader actions.

name: text
text: MongoDB stores accounts, stories, likes, follows, and saved items.

name: text
text: The website, server, and database each have a clear role.

The system has three parts. The presentation tier contains the pages readers use. The application tier handles requests such as search and article publishing. The data tier stores accounts, stories, and user activity. Uploaded images use GridFS storage linked to the database.

name: text
text: THE DAILY BRIEF: AI-POWERED NEWS PLATFORM
Visitors can browse and search public stories. Readers and writers need an account to save, like, follow, or publish. Admin reviewers handle articles held for review and reader reports.

Future work could generate a suitable image from an article topic, suggest related stories, improve image screening, and compare important factual claims with sources. These are planned improvements; they are not current platform features.
